lesson.title: How many in each slice?
lesson.subtitle: P4 pie-chart revision
lesson.objective: Share the total of a pie chart between its equal slices, then find the number in a group.
lesson.story: The pie chart shows 120 pupils in all, sorted into Apples, Pears, Grapes and Plums. Every slice stands for the same number of pupils.

steps.title: Find one slice
steps.prompt: The pie has 10 equal slices and shows 120 pupils in all. How many pupils does one slice stand for?
hints: Every slice stands for the same number.
Share the whole amount equally between all the slices.

steps.title: Count a group
steps.prompt: How many pupils are in the Plums group?
hints: Count the slices that Plums covers.
Each slice stands for the same number of pupils, so multiply.
Plums covers 3 slices and each slice stands for 12: work out 3 × 12.

steps.title: Find how many more
steps.prompt: How many more pupils are in the Plums group than in the Apples group?
hints: Find how many more slices Plums covers than Apples.
Count the slices of each group and take the smaller number from the larger.
Plums covers 3 slices and Apples covers 1, which is 2 more. Each slice stands for 12.

steps.title: Explain your thinking
steps.prompt: Why do we find what one slice stands for first?

choices.label: Every group stands for the same number, so the number of slices does not matter.
One slice always stands for 1, so the number of slices is the amount in a group.
Each slice stands for the same number, so count slices to find any group.

hints: Think about the slices of the pie.
All the slices are the same size.
Knowing one slice lets you work out any group.
Choose the explanation about counting slices.
